title: Dual-state fifth-moment necessity for modular cutoff locality
question: Does a uniform fifth moment of the reference Gibbs state and a relative form bound for a local multiplier suffice to make the opposite-side energy cutoff tail small, or is a dual-state moment required?

moment_and_tail.necessity: The reference fifth moment remains bounded while the opposite-side cutoff tail stays above 1/2 and the dual fifth moment grows like L^5. A dual-state or modular-energy tail is therefore a necessary extra input for this cutoff architecture.

scope.not_closed: The witness rejects only the one-sided reference-moment shortcut for an abstract finite Gibbs/cutoff family. It is not a counterexample to the actual Q3 local energy, its dual Gibbs states, or a stronger modular-tail theorem. All Q3 and QFT gates remain open.

adversarial_review.check: The rational state ratio rho_22/rho_11=L^-6 equals exp(-beta*(L-1)) for an explicit finite positive beta.
P_R and Q_R are exact spectral projections of k with R=2 and L>2; no arbitrary coordinate projection is substituted.
The swap multiplier has both squared relative graph norms at most one because k>=I; the bound is computed from singular values, not assumed from a scalar norm.
Reference and dual fifth moments are evaluated separately; the missing dual quantity is not silently identified with the reference moment.
The nonvanishing tail is the opposite-side quantity ||Q_R B rho^(1/2)||_2, exactly the side that requires B rho B^* energy control.
All fixtures use exact integer/rational arithmetic and the reference ceiling and tail floor are checked symbolically.
R261 checks rational Gibbs ratios, moments, tail identities and inequalities only; it does not formalize Q3.
The witness does not alter Q3 Hamiltonian/Gibbs, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or TECT production status.

qft_interface.closed: A finite Gibbs/cutoff witness proves that a reference fifth moment and a local relative bound do not by themselves control the opposite-side cutoff tail; a dual-state or modular-energy tail is mathematically necessary for this route.
qft_interface.open: Actual Q3 dual-state moment bounds, modular cutoff locality, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, first-passage history, exhaustion, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, common KMS dynamics, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: No heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.

next_action: Prove both one-sided/dual-state fifth-energy or modular-tail bounds for the actual Q3 projected bond on a predeclared faithful phase-pair/separating class; only then use the equilibrium cutoff alternative in direct D and delta-D convergence.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite dual-state modular-cutoff route obstruction.
